findings.title: Heartbeat timeout specifies illegal WebSocket close code 1006
findings.evidence: "Missed pong → close with 1006 (\"abnormal closure\") after 2 missed intervals."
findings.problem: The spec requires sending close code 1006, but RFC 6455 reserves 1006 for reporting abnormal closure and forbids sending it in a close frame.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementations will either fail, substitute a different code, or behave inconsistently across .NET WebSocket libraries, breaking heartbeat and reconnect behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace 1006 with a legal close behavior: either abort without a close frame on heartbeat failure, or send an allowed close code/custom 4xxx code and define client handling/tests for it.

findings.title: API-key lockout persistence is required without any defined schema
findings.location: SPEC-01 §12.6 Rate Limiting and Abuse Protection
findings.evidence: "10 failed attempts per hour → temporary key lockout (15 min), logged as an `api_keys.lockout_event` row (schema deferred to post-hackathon)."
findings.problem: The v1 auth contract requires writing lockout events, but no table/schema is defined for `api_keys.lockout_event`.
findings.why_it_matters: This cannot be implemented or migration-tested as written, and auth behavior will drift between environments.
findings.proposed_fix: Either define the lockout schema and migration now, or remove/defer the persistence requirement from the v1 contract.

findings.title: Cross-workstation conflict detection relies on an untrusted machine-name field
findings.location: SPEC-01 §5 AddinReadyMessage / SPEC-01 §9 AddinSessionId / SPEC-00 §3 Acceptance Test Cross-Reference
findings.evidence: "`WorkstationId`: `Environment.MachineName` ... is NOT a security trust boundary"; "Cross-workstation collision ... on a different `WorkstationId`"; "ACC-19 | Cross-workstation AddinSessionId conflict throws"
findings.problem: The hard-error conflict rule depends on `WorkstationId`, which is client-supplied and not guaranteed unique or trustworthy.
findings.why_it_matters: ACC-19 is not reliably enforceable, and same-tenant session conflicts can be misclassified or silently merged.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a stable persisted device/client-instance identifier with explicit uniqueness requirements, and base conflict detection on that identifier instead of `Environment.MachineName`.

findings.title: Viewer dependency graph is contradictory across specs
findings.location: SPEC-00 §1 Module Map / SPEC-01 §18 Consumption by Other Specs
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 lists `SPEC-06 | Viewer | Depends On | SPEC-04 (read-only)`; SPEC-01 states `"SPEC-06 imports StateSnapshot, SelectionRef, FeatureNode"`.
findings.problem: SPEC-06 is declared to depend only on SPEC-04, but another spec requires it to import SPEC-01 types.
findings.why_it_matters: Architecture tests, project references, and packaging cannot satisfy both statements; this will cause immediate repo-shape churn.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one contract: either expose viewer-needed DTOs entirely via SPEC-04 read models, or explicitly allow SPEC-06 to depend on SPEC-01 and update the dependency rules/tests.

findings.title: Viewer capability-based session listing has no matching read-only repository API
findings.evidence: "Session listing requires possession of a valid session UUID as capability proof"; "knowing one session UUID for a tenant reveals all sessions for that tenant via the sidebar"; `ListSessionsAsync(string tenantId, CancellationToken ct = default)`
findings.problem: The viewer access model is based on a session UUID capability, but the read-only repository only offers tenant-based listing and defines no way to authorize or derive that listing from the session capability.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-06 cannot implement the sidebar contract cleanly without bypassing the repository or introducing undocumented tenant-resolution logic.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a read-only method that accepts a capability sessionId and returns the authorized tenant session list, or explicitly define the tenant-resolution and authorization flow from sessionId.

findings.title: CallId is validated as UUIDv7 without any protocol-level format definition
findings.location: SPEC-02 §6.5 MessageDispatcher / SPEC-02 §10 Required Tests / SPEC-01 §5 Message Record Definitions
findings.evidence: SPEC-02: `"MessageDispatcher validates that CallId conforms to the UUIDv7 format"` and `CallIdFormatValidationTests`; SPEC-01 defines `CallId` only as `"Lifecycle identity (see SPEC-03)"`.
findings.problem: The add-in rejects `CallId` values based on a format rule that the wire protocol never declares.
findings.why_it_matters: Producer and consumer implementations can disagree while both remain spec-compliant, causing avoidable protocol failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the canonical `CallId` format and validation rules in SPEC-01, or remove UUIDv7-specific validation from SPEC-02.

findings.title: Recovery-event append path drops PNG bytes added to the new DHF schema
findings.evidence: `RecoveryEventContext` includes `byte[]? ScreenshotBeforePng` and `byte[]? ScreenshotAfterPng`, but `AppendRecoveryEventAsync` builds `DhfTurnContext` with `ScreenshotBeforePath = null`, `ScreenshotAfterPath = null`, and copies only SHA256 fields.
findings.problem: The specified write path never carries the PNG bytes into persistence, so `dhf.entries.screenshot_before_png` and `screenshot_after_png` cannot be populated for recovery events.
findings.why_it_matters: The new screenshot BYTEA columns remain unusable for recovery entries, so deep validation and viewer screenshot rendering are still incomplete.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend `DhfTurnContext`/append logic to include PNG byte payloads, or add a dedicated recovery-entry insert path that writes the BYTEA columns and test it.

findings.title: Duplicate ToolCall behavior is unspecified despite reconnect-scoped dedup cache
findings.evidence: Project shape: `"ToolCallRegistry.cs # In-flight dedup + 60s result cache (session-scoped)"`; §6.6 only defines tracker states and says the registry survives reconnects.
findings.problem: The spec does not define what the add-in must do when a duplicate `ToolCallMessage` arrives for a `CallId` in `Queued`, `Executing`, `Completed`, `Cancelled`, or `Abandoned`, or after the 60s cache expires.
findings.why_it_matters: Reconnect/idempotency behavior will diverge across implementations and can cause duplicate COM mutations or nondeterministic failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify per-state duplicate handling, replay vs reject rules, cache TTL start/eviction semantics, and add explicit tests for each state.

findings.title: ACC-20 performance gate is not reproducible
findings.evidence: "ACC-20 | Viewer timeline renders a 20-entry session in under 1 second on the demo laptop"
findings.problem: The acceptance criterion does not define the benchmark hardware, browser, cache state, network conditions, or measurement point.
findings.why_it_matters: CI and manual acceptance cannot produce a deterministic pass/fail result, so performance regressions will be disputed instead of caught.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the exact benchmark fixture and measurement method, including hardware profile, browser/runtime, warm vs cold cache, and whether the 1s target is server, network, or UI render time.
